title: Not east or west
hook: righteousness is not turning your face east or west, but belief, giving, keeping promises, patience (2:177)

segments.voice: Yesterday: signs for those who think. What ordinary thing did you look at a little longer? Today, the end of a week, and a verse that looks at people the way yesterday's looked at clouds. Day three hundred fifty.

A few pages back, al-Baqarah told of the qiblah turning: the direction of prayer moved from Jerusalem to Mecca, and some people argued about it loudly. Which way is right? Which way is holy? Who was wrong all those years? An argument about a direction can run for a long time without anyone having to change how they live. Then, further on in the same surah, the verse steps over the whole argument with one sentence. Today: birr.
screen: `THE QIBLAH TURNED.` → `WHICH WAY IS RIGHT?` → `ONE SENTENCE STEPS OVER IT.`

segments.voice: Verse one hundred seventy-seven, in Pickthall's words: “It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West.” The word is birr: righteousness, goodness, devotion. It's the same word Muslims use for kindness to parents, birr al-walidayn. Then the verse says what birr is, and it's a long, concrete list. Belief: in God, the Last Day, the angels, the book, the prophets. Giving wealth, though you love it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and to free those in bondage. Establishing the prayer and paying the zakat. Keeping your promises when you make them. And patience in poverty, in sickness, and in the moment of danger. Commentators read one phrase two ways. Giving wealth 'ala hubbihi can mean despite loving it, or out of love for God. Both readings have their teachers. Notice the verse doesn't say direction doesn't matter. Muslims still face the Kaaba when they pray. It says that facing the right way isn't, by itself, goodness. Goodness is belief that shows up as giving, praying, keeping your word, and holding steady when things go wrong. Look back at the week. Builders who prayed for people not yet born. A father asking what his sons would keep. A middle people. Remembrance, loss, the clouds. Each day was a piece of this one list. Righteousness is what you do.
screen: `NOT EAST, NOT WEST` · `BIRR: GOODNESS, DEVOTION` · `BELIEF, GIVING, PROMISES, PATIENCE` · `THE WEEK, IN ONE LIST`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: keep one promise today. Sit, and think back over the last week. What did you say you'd do? Call back, send the file, fix the shelf, visit, pay someone back. Find one you haven't kept yet. Picture yourself keeping it, today, in the plainest way. Then let the breath settle, and hold the decision quietly, like something already done. The bell holds the time.
Birr. Righteousness, goodness, devotion. Al-Baqarah says it's not facing east or west, but belief, giving, prayer, keeping promises, and patience. Today's word.
Your line: righteousness is what you do. Today, keep the promise you found, before the day ends, even if it is small and nobody but you remembers it. Day three hundred fifty.

howItsDone: Muslims often cite 2:177 as a summary of faith in practice: belief together with charity, prayer, zakat, keeping promises and patience; the same word, birr, names kindness to parents.
